---
title: "Setup test: R and Python"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
---

This document checks that Quarto can run R and Python code on your computer. Each check prints the answer it expects and the answer it got. Save it in a subfolder of your project, such as `analysis/`, and render it.

R adds the numbers 1 to 10.

```{r}
#| label: r-check
cat("R runs: expected 55, got", sum(1:10), "\n")
```

The `here` package looks for the project folder: the nearest folder, at or above this one, that holds the `.here` file.

```{r}
#| label: here-check
cat(".here file in the project folder: expected TRUE, got",
    file.exists(here::here(".here")), "\n")
cat("project folder:", here::here(), "\n")
```

Python adds the numbers 1 to 10, then prints the path of the Python program that ran it.

```{python}
#| label: python-check
import sys
print("Python runs: expected 55, got", sum(range(1, 11)))
print("Python used:", sys.executable)
```
